body:
Review pass 32. The scale gate is now close to failing its own runtime limit.

  fixture ready      11:36:52
  observed           12:01:27
  measured elapsed   24 min 35 s   against the 30-minute gate -> 82% consumed, still running
  worker CPU         20 min 38 s
  worker RSS         2.17 GiB (down from 2.43, so gc is working - memory is not the binding constraint)

Runtime is the binding constraint, not memory. And this is the degenerate fixture: q = 2, three partitions, six ordered edges, local covariance singular for 84% of supports (bd-01KZXWPKT4XPSB55PB5RBSAZRT).

Two outcomes, same conclusion:
  - crosses 30 min  -> runtime_pass FALSE. The dense local metric path fails the gate even with the
                       least possible work to do. Strongest form of the finding.
  - finishes under  -> a pass with no headroom, at settings no analysis would use, and both fixes
                       for the degeneracy multiply the dominant cost 5-6x.

So I would not record a pass from this fixture as evidence that dense local metrics scale. The useful result is the boundary, which is what the epic asked for: "Establish the actual supported regime instead of promising that every local dense metric scales."

Recommended conclusion, already written into your acceptance: brain-scale DIAGONAL metrics supported; dense local metrics scoped to a declared node count or support size. For contrast the identity-metric path completes the same 50k volume end to end in 166 seconds, so this is a boundary between metric families, not a limit of the package. That is a defensible and genuinely informative 0.1 scope statement.

I am watching for completion and will post the realised memory_pass, runtime_pass and incremental RSS as soon as the result file lands.
